title: SOC Analyst
summary: Monitor, triage and investigate security alerts with SIEM, KQL and ATT&CK, through six hands-on investigation labs.
description: A practical programme for people preparing for security operations roles. You will learn how a SOC works, read Windows, Linux, network and cloud telemetry, write KQL for investigation and detection, triage alerts across multiple sources, map behaviour to MITRE ATT&CK, and document incidents professionally. Every concept is practised in simulated investigations built on synthetic data, so you need no paid cloud subscription.
audience: IT support and service desk professionals moving into security
Network and system administrators who handle security alerts
prerequisites: Comfortable using a computer and web browser
Basic understanding of what IP addresses and operating systems are
outcomes: Triage alerts with a repeatable, documented method
Interpret Windows Security, Linux authentication and DNS evidence
Write KQL queries to investigate and detect suspicious activity
Map observed behaviour to MITRE ATT&CK techniques
Build and test detection logic against known-good and known-bad data
Write case notes, escalations and incident reports
inclusions: Digital badge and verifiable certificate on completion
Access to course version 1 for the period set out in the terms

faqs.q: Do I need a Microsoft Sentinel subscription?
faqs.a: No. All KQL labs run in AMANIQ's built-in simulator over synthetic data. The syntax you learn is standard KQL and transfers directly to Microsoft Sentinel.

faqs.q: Is this certificate a professional certification?
faqs.a: No. You receive a certificate of completion issued by AMANIQ Academy. It is not an external or government-accredited qualification and is not affiliated with any vendor certification.
We estimate around 60 hours including labs. Your pace may differ.

faqs.q: What do I need to pass?
faqs.a: Complete all required lessons, pass all six labs, and score at least 75% (30 of 40) on the final examination.

badge.name: AMANIQ SOC Analyst
badge.description: Awarded for completing the AMANIQ Academy SOC Analyst programme.
badge.criteria: Completed all required lessons, passed all six labs and scored at least 75% on the final examination.

modules.title: Cybersecurity Operations Fundamentals
modules.purpose: Establish what a SOC does, the vocabulary analysts use, and how alerts move from detection to escalation.
modules.prerequisiteKnowledge: General IT literacy. No prior security experience required.
objectives: Describe the core responsibilities of a SOC and common team structures.
Distinguish events, alerts and incidents, and classify alert outcomes correctly.
Assign severity using documented criteria and write a complete escalation message.
assessmentCriteria: Correctly classifies alert outcomes in scenario questions
Produces an escalation note containing severity, facts, scope, actions and the decision required
modules.instructorNotes: Encourage learners to find real SOC runbook templates published by public bodies and compare them with the escalation format taught here.

lessons.title: What a SOC does and how it works
objectives: Explain the three questions every SOC answers
Describe the alert lifecycle and why every closure needs a reason

checks.question: An analyst closes an alert with the note "Closed". What is the main problem?
options: Nothing; closing quickly is the goal
Without a reason, the alert cannot inform tuning or review
Alerts must never be closed by Tier 1
The alert should have been deleted instead
checks.explanation: Closure reasons feed detection tuning and make decisions reviewable.

lessons.title: Events, alerts and incidents
objectives: Define event, alert and incident precisely
Classify alert outcomes including benign true positives

checks.question: A rule detecting PsExec fires during an approved maintenance window run by IT. What is the best classification?
checks.explanation: The rule detected exactly the behaviour it targets, but the activity was authorised.

lessons.title: Severity, priority and escalation
objectives: Apply severity criteria to scenarios
Write an escalation message that requests a specific decision

checks.question: Which element is most important to include in an escalation message to a decision-maker?
options: The specific decision or approval you need
A screenshot of the SIEM dashboard
checks.explanation: Escalations exist to obtain authority or expertise; state exactly what you need.

modules.title: Networking and Operating System Telemetry
modules.purpose: Give analysts fluency in the network, Windows and Linux evidence they read every day.
modules.prerequisiteKnowledge: Module 1. Basic familiarity with IP addresses is helpful.
objectives: Interpret TCP/IP, port and DNS evidence in logs.
Identify key Windows Security event IDs and logon types.
Read Linux authentication logs and account for time-zone differences.
assessmentCriteria: Identifies spraying versus brute force from authentication logs
Converts local syslog times to UTC correctly

lessons.title: TCP/IP and DNS for analysts
objectives: Recognise common ports and their analyst relevance
Spot suspicious DNS query patterns

checks.question: A workstation makes TXT queries every 60 seconds to random-looking subdomains of one domain. What does this most suggest?
checks.explanation: Regular timing, random subdomains and TXT records together are classic tunnelling/beaconing indicators.

lessons.title: Windows event logging
objectives: Recall the meaning of key Security event IDs
Interpret logon types and failure status codes

checks.question: Event 4625 with SubStatus 0xC0000064 indicates what?
options: Wrong password for a valid user
checks.explanation: 0xC0000064 means the user name does not exist; 0xC000006A means a bad password for a valid user.

checks.question: Which logon type corresponds to RDP?
checks.explanation: Logon type 10 is RemoteInteractive, used by Remote Desktop.

lessons.title: Linux authentication and system logs
objectives: Read sshd and sudo log lines
Normalise local syslog timestamps to UTC

checks.question: A Lagos server (UTC+1) logs "Mar 4 03:01:12". What is the time in UTC?
options: It cannot be determined in principle
checks.explanation: West Africa Time is UTC+1, so subtract one hour.

modules.title: SIEM Architecture and Log Analysis
modules.purpose: Explain how a SIEM collects, normalises and correlates data, and how detection quality is managed.
objectives: Describe each stage of a SIEM pipeline and the role of normalisation.
Design correlation logic in plain language before writing queries.
Apply safe tuning techniques and explain the risk of broad exclusions.
assessmentCriteria: Identifies missed events caused by lookback windows
Chooses a narrow, documented exclusion over a broad one

lessons.title: Collection, parsing and normalisation
objectives: Explain why normalisation enables cross-source detection
Distinguish 'no results' from 'no data'

checks.question: Your query for failed logons returns no rows. What should you check first?
options: That the data source is present for that time range
Whether the SIEM licence is expired
Rewrite the query in another language
checks.explanation: Absence of results only means something if the data was collected.

lessons.title: Correlation and detection rules
objectives: Compare detection logic types
Set lookback windows that tolerate ingestion delay

checks.question: A rule runs every 5 minutes with a 5-minute lookback. Events typically arrive 3 minutes late. What happens?
options: Some events can be missed between runs
checks.explanation: Lookback must exceed frequency plus expected delay.

lessons.title: False positives, tuning and alert quality
objectives: Measure alert quality
Tune detections without creating blind spots

checks.question: Which exclusion is safest?
options: Exclude one scanner host for one process, with an owner and expiry
checks.explanation: Narrow, documented, time-limited exclusions minimise blind spots.

modules.title: Microsoft Sentinel and KQL Fundamentals
modules.purpose: Build practical KQL skills for investigation and detection, usable in Microsoft Sentinel and Defender advanced hunting.
modules.prerequisiteKnowledge: Modules 1–3. No Microsoft subscription required: labs use the AMANIQ KQL simulator.
objectives: Filter and shape data with where, project and extend.
Aggregate with summarize, dcount, min/max and bin().
Explain joins and time-window analysis, and write performant, readable queries.
assessmentCriteria: Writes a query that distinguishes password spraying from brute force
Selects the correct join kind for a scenario
modules.instructorNotes: The simulator implements a documented subset (no join/let). Point learners to the Microsoft KQL reference for full syntax.

lessons.title: Tables, filters and columns
objectives: Write filtering queries with correct operators
Apply time filters early

checks.question: Which operator performs a case-insensitive equality test in KQL?
checks.explanation: =~ is case-insensitive equality; == is case-sensitive.

lessons.title: Summarising and aggregating
objectives: Use summarize with dcount to separate attack patterns
Build time series with bin()

checks.question: One IP has failures against 300 different users. Which aggregation revealed this?
checks.explanation: dcount of the user column shows how many distinct accounts were targeted, the signature of spraying.

checks.question: What is KQL's default sort direction for order by?
checks.explanation: Unlike SQL, KQL sorts descending by default.

lessons.title: Joins, time analysis and query performance
objectives: Choose join kinds correctly
Apply performance best practices

checks.question: To list assets that did NOT send logs today, which join kind fits best?
checks.explanation: leftanti returns left rows with no match on the right.

modules.title: Alert Triage and Investigation
modules.purpose: Teach a repeatable triage and investigation method that produces defensible conclusions.
objectives: Follow a structured triage sequence for any alert.
Record evidence that separates fact from interpretation.
Enrich entities and build a UTC investigation timeline.
assessmentCriteria: Reaches the correct verdict on a multi-source alert
Produces a timeline with evidence references

lessons.title: Alert validation and evidence collection
objectives: Apply the six-step triage sequence
Document evidence reproducibly

checks.question: Why should analysts record the time range of every query?
options: So others can reproduce and verify the result
checks.explanation: Reproducibility is what makes a finding evidence.

lessons.title: Entity enrichment and timelines
objectives: Enrich users, hosts, IPs, domains and hashes
Build and test a timeline hypothesis

checks.question: A newly registered domain has a 'clean' reputation score. What should you conclude?
options: Reputation is one input; new domains often have no reports yet
checks.explanation: Absence of bad reputation is weak evidence, especially for new infrastructure.

modules.title: MITRE ATT&CK and Detection Engineering
modules.purpose: Use ATT&CK to describe behaviour and plan coverage, and apply engineering discipline to detections.
objectives: Map observed behaviour to ATT&CK tactics and techniques.
Assess detection coverage distinguishing data, detection and validation.
Read Sigma rules and express detection logic in KQL.
assessmentCriteria: Maps a timeline to correct technique IDs
Builds a detection that passes known-good and known-bad tests

lessons.title: Working with MITRE ATT&CK
objectives: Explain TTPs
Map evidence to techniques and record the ATT&CK version

checks.question: Password spraying maps to which ATT&CK technique?
checks.explanation: Password spraying is sub-technique .003 of T1110 Brute Force.

lessons.title: Detection logic and Sigma
objectives: Read a Sigma rule
Increase precision through combined conditions

checks.question: Which detection is most specific?
checks.explanation: Combining independent conditions that rarely co-occur legitimately raises precision.

modules.title: Threat Intelligence and Hunting
modules.purpose: Evaluate intelligence critically and run structured, hypothesis-driven hunts.
objectives: Judge indicator quality by source, context, confidence, age and relevance.
Manage IOC expiry and avoid blocking shared infrastructure.
Plan and execute a hypothesis-driven hunt and record its outcomes.
assessmentCriteria: Prioritises indicators correctly in scenarios
Writes a testable hunting hypothesis

lessons.title: Indicators and intelligence quality
objectives: Assess indicator quality
Apply IOC hygiene

checks.question: Why should IP-address indicators have an expiry date?
options: Attacker infrastructure is recycled and later used by innocent parties
checks.explanation: Old IP indicators cause false positives on reassigned addresses.

lessons.title: Hypothesis-driven threat hunting
objectives: Write testable hypotheses
Turn hunt outcomes into detections and baselines

checks.question: A hunt finds no intrusion. Which outcome still makes it valuable?
options: A new baseline, detection or documented data gap
checks.explanation: Hunts improve visibility and detection even when nothing malicious is found.

modules.title: Endpoint Security and Incident Response
modules.purpose: Read endpoint evidence and coordinate containment, eradication and recovery.
objectives: Identify suspicious process trees and persistence mechanisms.
Recognise early ransomware-operation indicators.
Select containment actions appropriate to the threat and evidence needs.
assessmentCriteria: Identifies persistence from registry evidence
Sequences containment after scoping

lessons.title: EDR, suspicious processes and persistence
objectives: Read process trees
Detect persistence mechanisms

checks.question: A Run key named OneDriveSync points to AppData\Roaming\upd\updater.exe. What is the key finding?
options: The value name imitates a legitimate product but the path does not match it
checks.explanation: Masquerading names with mismatched binary paths are a strong persistence indicator.

lessons.title: Containment, eradication and recovery
objectives: Choose containment strategies
Explain post-incident review and legal escalation

checks.question: Why scope before resetting a compromised account's password?
options: The attacker may hold other accounts and will be alerted
checks.explanation: Coordinated containment avoids tipping off an attacker who retains other access.

modules.title: Incident Documentation and SOC Reporting
modules.purpose: Produce case notes, handovers, metrics and incident reports that stand up to review.
objectives: Write case notes, evidence registers and handover notes.
Select SOC metrics that avoid perverse incentives.
Structure an incident report for multiple audiences.
assessmentCriteria: Produces a handover note another analyst can act on
Writes an executive summary free of raw log data

lessons.title: Case notes, evidence and handover
objectives: Maintain case notes as you work
Preserve evidence integrity

checks.question: Why record SHA-256 hashes of exported evidence files?
checks.explanation: A matching hash shows the file has not changed since collection.

lessons.title: Metrics and incident reporting
objectives: Choose meaningful metrics
Structure a professional incident report

checks.question: When should the executive summary of an incident report be written?
options: Last, once the evidence is understood
checks.explanation: Write it last so it reflects exactly what the evidence supports.

modules.title: Detection Engineering Capstone
modules.purpose: Integrate detection, investigation, documentation and reporting on a realistic simulated incident.
objectives: Build and test detection logic against synthetic data.
Investigate a multi-stage intrusion across several telemetry sources.
Produce a professional incident report.
assessmentCriteria: Passes Labs 4 and 6
Self-assesses the incident report against the checklist

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the difference between an alert and an incident?

options.text: An alert is a hypothesis that needs triage; an incident is a confirmed problem requiring response
Incidents are generated automatically; alerts are reported by users
Alerts only come from antivirus software

questions.explanation: Alerts are notifications that need validation; incidents are confirmed.

questions.prompt: A vulnerability scanner on its approved schedule triggers a port-scan detection. How should the alert be classified?

options.text: False positive caused by a broken rule

questions.explanation: The rule detected scanning correctly, but the activity is authorised.

questions.prompt: Which outcome category represents the greatest hidden risk to a SOC?
questions.explanation: False negatives are malicious activity that produced no alert, so nobody sees them.

questions.prompt: Which factor most strongly justifies raising an incident to the highest severity?

options.text: The alert fired outside business hours
Confirmed exfiltration of sensitive personal data
The source IP is in another country
The user is new to the organisation

questions.explanation: Confirmed loss of sensitive data meets critical criteria.

questions.prompt: Which TWO elements should appear in every escalation message?

options.text: The decision or approval you need
A concise statement of facts and scope

questions.explanation: Escalations must be concise, factual and ask for a specific decision.

questions.prompt: Which Windows Security event ID records a failed logon?
questions.explanation: 4625 is 'An account failed to log on'.

questions.prompt: A successful 4624 logon shows LogonType 10 from an unfamiliar workstation. What does this indicate?
questions.explanation: Logon type 10 is RemoteInteractive, i.e. RDP.

questions.prompt: Many 4625 events from one source show SubStatus 0xC000006A across different users. What can you infer?

options.text: The attacker is using valid usernames with wrong passwords

questions.explanation: 0xC000006A means a valid user with a bad password.

questions.prompt: On Ubuntu, where are SSH authentication events typically written by rsyslog?
questions.explanation: Debian/Ubuntu use auth.log; RHEL uses /var/log/secure.

questions.prompt: A classic syslog line from a server in UTC+1 reads 'Mar 4 07:30:00'. What must you do before correlating it with UTC cloud logs?

options.text: Convert it to 06:30:00 UTC and confirm the year
Discard it, as syslog lacks time zones

questions.explanation: Classic syslog has no year or offset; convert local time to UTC.

questions.prompt: Which pattern in DNS logs is most suggestive of tunnelling?

options.text: A workstation resolving its file server
Hundreds of queries to unique random subdomains of one domain from a single host
NXDOMAIN for a mistyped intranet name

questions.explanation: High-entropy unique subdomains under one parent domain are typical of tunnelling.

questions.prompt: Why does a SIEM normalise fields from different log sources?

options.text: So one detection rule can work across products that name fields differently

questions.explanation: Normalisation maps vendor fields to a common schema.

questions.prompt: A scheduled rule runs every 10 minutes. Data arrives up to 4 minutes late. What lookback avoids gaps?
questions.explanation: Lookback must cover frequency plus delay.

questions.prompt: 'Many failed logons followed by a success from the same IP' is an example of which detection type?
questions.explanation: It combines different events in sequence.

questions.prompt: Which tuning action creates the largest blind spot?

options.text: Fixing a substring that matched unintended values
Excluding an entire administrative subnet permanently
Raising a threshold based on 30 days of data

questions.explanation: Broad permanent exclusions hide exactly the hosts attackers want.

questions.objective: Distinguish no data from no results
questions.prompt: A hunting query returns zero rows. What should you verify first?

options.text: That the relevant data source was ingested for that period
That the analyst has admin rights
That the SIEM is licensed for hunting
Nothing; zero rows means no threat

questions.explanation: No results only matters if the data exists.

questions.prompt: Which KQL operator matches a value case-insensitively for equality?
questions.explanation: =~ is case-insensitive equality.

questions.prompt: In KQL, what is the default direction of 'order by'?
questions.explanation: KQL sorts descending unless asc is specified.

questions.prompt: Which query best identifies password-spraying sources?

options.text: SigninLogs | where ResultType != "0" | summarize dcount(UserPrincipalName) by IPAddress

questions.explanation: Distinct targeted users per source reveals spraying.

questions.prompt: What does 'summarize count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)' produce?

options.text: Hourly counts suitable for spotting spikes
The first hour of data only
An error, because bin needs a number

questions.explanation: bin() buckets timestamps into fixed intervals.

questions.prompt: You need users who signed in but have NO matching MFA registration record. Which join kind fits?
questions.explanation: leftanti returns left rows with no right-side match.

questions.prompt: Which TWO practices improve KQL performance in production?

options.text: Prefer has over contains for whole-term matches
Search all tables with * in every scheduled rule

questions.explanation: Early time filters and term-indexed operators reduce work.

questions.prompt: What should an analyst do immediately after reading the alert definition?

options.text: Identify the entities involved (user, host, IP, process)

questions.explanation: Entities are the pivots for every later step.

questions.prompt: Which case-note entry is most useful as evidence?

options.text: Queried SigninLogs for 203.0.113.45, 00:00–06:00 UTC: 212 failures, 1 success; assessed as spraying

questions.explanation: It records query, range, result and labelled interpretation.

questions.prompt: Why might rebooting a suspected compromised host be harmful?

options.text: It destroys volatile evidence such as memory contents

questions.explanation: Memory evidence is lost on reboot.

questions.prompt: Why should analysts be cautious about uploading internal files to public sandboxes?

options.text: It may disclose confidential data and alert the attacker

questions.explanation: Public submission can leak data and reveal detection.

questions.prompt: An analyst decides early that an alert is benign and only seeks confirming evidence. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Anchoring bias distorts triage.

questions.prompt: In ATT&CK, what does a tactic represent?

options.text: The adversary's goal at a stage, such as Persistence

questions.explanation: Tactics are the 'why'; techniques are the 'how'.

questions.prompt: An attacker creates an inbox rule forwarding mail to an external address. Which technique fits best?

options.text: T1114.003 Email Collection: Email Forwarding Rule

questions.explanation: Forwarding rules are a sub-technique of Email Collection.

questions.prompt: Which statement about ATT&CK coverage is most accurate?

options.text: Having a rule for a technique means it is covered
Coverage should distinguish data available, detection exists and detection validated
Coverage of 100% of techniques is the goal for every organisation

questions.explanation: Untested rules overstate protection.

questions.prompt: What is Sigma?

options.text: A vendor-neutral YAML format for describing log detections

questions.explanation: Sigma rules can be converted to many SIEM query languages.

questions.prompt: Which detection logic is most specific for malicious documents?

options.text: powershell.exe or cmd.exe whose parent is winword.exe, excel.exe or powerpnt.exe

questions.explanation: Requiring the Office parent removes most benign matches.

questions.prompt: Before enabling a new detection, which TWO test sets should it be run against?
questions.explanation: It must fire on bad and stay quiet on good.

questions.prompt: Which indicator type is generally easiest for an attacker to change?
questions.explanation: Hashes sit at the bottom of the Pyramid of Pain.

questions.prompt: An IP indicator was last observed 14 months ago. What is the main risk of blocking it now?

options.text: It may now belong to an innocent party, causing false positives

questions.explanation: IP infrastructure is recycled; indicators need expiry.

questions.prompt: Which is a well-formed hunting hypothesis?

options.text: If an attacker uses DNS tunnelling, a host will query many unique subdomains of one domain

questions.explanation: A hypothesis is testable and names the expected telemetry.

questions.prompt: Which audience is strategic threat intelligence mainly for?
questions.explanation: Strategic intelligence informs business decisions.

questions.prompt: Which TWO are valuable outcomes of a hunt that found no intrusion?

options.text: A documented baseline of normal behaviour

questions.explanation: Hunts improve detection and visibility.

questions.prompt: Which location is a common Windows persistence mechanism?
questions.explanation: Run keys start programs at logon (T1547.001).

questions.prompt: Which observation is most suspicious?

options.text: svchost.exe started by services.exe from System32
svchost.exe running from a user's Downloads folder

questions.explanation: System binary names in user-writable paths indicate masquerading.

questions.prompt: Which activity is an early indicator of a ransomware operation before encryption?
questions.explanation: Removing recovery options typically precedes encryption.

questions.prompt: Why should credential resets usually be coordinated after scoping?

options.text: The attacker may hold other accounts and will be alerted

questions.explanation: Partial containment tips off the attacker.

questions.prompt: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 aligns incident response with which framework?
questions.explanation: Rev. 3 (2025) maps IR activities to CSF 2.0 Functions.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of recording a SHA-256 hash of exported evidence?

options.text: Demonstrate the file has not changed since collection

questions.explanation: Hashes support integrity and chain of custody.

questions.prompt: Which metric is most likely to create a perverse incentive if used alone?

options.text: Alerts closed per analyst per hour

questions.explanation: It rewards fast, careless closure.

questions.prompt: What belongs in an incident report's executive summary?

options.text: What happened, the impact, current status and key recommendations

questions.explanation: The summary is for non-technical decision-makers.
